appearance_facts.fact: Product A bar is the shortest of the five bars; its top sits just below the 2,000 gridline, clearly lower than Product C's top which sits just above 2,000.
Five dark-red vertical bars are arranged left-to-right in the order Product E, Product A, Product C, Product D, Product B.
Y-axis ticks are labeled 2,000, 4,000, 6,000, 8,000, 10,000 from bottom to top; the Product A bar height is below the 2,000 tick.
Product D reaches the 10,000 line (tallest); Product E is near 8,000; Product B is at 6,000; Product C is just above 2,000; Product A is just below 2,000 (shortest).

printed_facts.fact: Title reads 'Units Sold by Product (Weekend Pop-up)'.
Axis label 'Product'; category labels Product E, Product A, Product C, Product D, Product B.
Row: '>= 1,000 and < 2,000 units' → 'Low-sales review queue activation level'.
Row: '< 500 units from a decision threshold' → 'Manual merchandising verification variance band'.
Row: '>= 6,000 and < 9,000 units' → 'Expanded replenishment planning level'.

public_definitions: Primary field: 'Merchandising route'; review product is 'Product A'; review program is 'Weekend pop-up merchandising review'.

Option set includes: Open Product A low-sales review; Route Product A to critical sales escalation; Keep Product A on regular merchandising plan; Route Product A to expanded replenishment planning; Route Product A to growth allocation review; Flag Product A for manual merchandising check.
Instructions: 'Use the Units Sold by Product dashboard as the evidence source for the Product A merchandising route.'
Policy mapping ties unit ranges to named merchandising route levels (critical escalation, low-sales review, manual verification band, expanded replenishment, growth allocation).
uncertain: Exact numeric value of the Product A bar is not printed; it is read visually as just below the 2,000 tick, placing it in the 1,000–2,000 band, but the precise figure (e.g., ~1,800) is an estimate.
Whether the '< 500 units from a decision threshold' manual-verification band applies to Product A depends on an unspecified 'decision threshold' value that is not shown on the dashboard.
